title.en: Navigable density with visual rest areas

summary: Organize a dense scene into readable clusters, low-demand rest views and bounded navigation targets so exploration reveals detail without trapping the camera or erasing hierarchy.
objective: A viewer can enter, inspect and leave every required dense cluster, recover orientation at quieter views, and use alternate controls without relying on one pointer gesture.
applies_when: Many objects, labels or routes compete in one navigable scene.
Free orbit or pan can strand the camera inside geometry or far from meaningful targets.
intent_signals: add quiet overview rest areas between clusters
stop orbit camera getting lost in clutter
example_prompts: Compose a dense night market into inspectable clusters with quiet overview landings and resettable targets.
Make a service graph navigable with cluster focus, keyboard-accessible alternatives and a stable home view.
negative_signals: Filling every empty region with secondary props.
Calling unlimited orbit controls safe navigation without target or distance checks.
not_for: A sparse scene whose problem is insufficient content rather than navigation.

principles: Rest is relational, not empty by rule: a quieter view reduces competing contrast, labels or motion long enough to recover hierarchy. Its visual style can remain rich.
Partition density by meaningful clusters and routes. Each cluster needs a stable target, entry view and exit/recovery path; free exploration remains an option rather than the only path.
Navigation constraints protect required views and model boundaries without turning the experience into a rigid tour. Provide visible home/focus actions and a non-pointer route to primary targets.
implementation: In Blender, author named cluster collections, target empties, candidate home/rest cameras and coarse camera-clearance volumes. Do not treat object collections as a DOM focus order.

In Three.js, map targets to stable IDs and configure OrbitControls target and scene-specific pan/rotate/zoom plus distance/target-radius bounds. Add collision or camera-volume logic separately when solid boundaries matter; OrbitControls does not provide it.

Expose home, previous focus and cluster list actions. When crossing into a cluster, reduce or regroup labels/motion according to the presentation profile while keeping selection and world state intact.
observable_checks: From home, reach each required cluster and return using pointer and the declared keyboard/button alternative. Continuous physically framed routes do not unintentionally pass through solid geometry; authored cuts, portals or scale transitions may cross when clearly presented as display-only.
Attempt extreme zoom, pan and target changes: declared bounds or recovery controls prevent a lost view, and reset returns to the saved home state.
At each rest view, the primary landmark and next actions remain clear at supported viewport sizes; hidden details remain discoverable rather than deleted.

creative_affordances: Rest areas may be courtyards, blank margins, dark pauses, slow-motion zones or uncluttered overview states.
Dense clusters can remain exuberant when routes and hierarchy are legible.
known_limits: OrbitControls supplies orbit/dolly/pan and configurable limits but not collision avoidance, semantic target order or accessibility conformance.
Camera-clearance volumes and rest thresholds are scene-specific authored guidance.
No navigation, keyboard, collision or viewport test was run.

claims.statement: Three.js OrbitControls orbits around a target, supports orbiting, dollying and panning, exposes enable switches and distance/target-radius limits, and can save and reset camera-control state.
claims.scope: Current addon mechanics; collision avoidance, semantic navigation order, focus management and alternate UI remain application responsibilities.

source_refs.locator: Class description; target; enablePan/Rotate/Zoom; distance and target-radius limits; saveState/reset
